key_insight: HierDTA combines hierarchical drug structures and protein binding-site information to improve drug–target affinity prediction.
clinical_relevance: The framework could help prioritize compounds for cancer-relevant kinase targets before experimental testing, but clinical benefit has not been established.
method: Represents drugs as atom–motif graphs, propagating functional-motif information to atoms.
Models kinase-domain structures as residue interaction graphs and links drug–protein features through cross-attention.
Adds molecular fingerprints and pretrained ESM-2 embeddings for complementary global information.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports leading performance across all evaluated Davis metrics, the highest KIBA r_m² of 0.791, and a 21.7% MSE reduction in KIBA’s unseen-protein setting.
watch_item: Benchmark and virtual-screening results require prospective experimental validation before use in cancer drug development.
paper_title: HierDTA: Hierarchical Structure-Aware Representation Learning for Drug--Target Affinity Prediction
